line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2
teaches: In a fianchetto system, answer a harmless flank pawn poke by simply continuing your development, not by reacting to it — spending a move to prevent a pin would weaken a key square for no real gain.
explains: The bishop completes its fianchetto on g2, aimed down the long diagonal. You could burn a move to stop the coming pin — but that would only soften the b4 square for nothing. Just develop, and let the opponent's little rook-pawn nudge be the wasted move.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O
teaches: The instinctive supporting pawn move is not always best — castling first keeps a tempo in hand for when the pin is traded off, and leaves a tactical resource if the opponent gets greedy.
explains: The natural move is d3 to prop the centre — but castling is stronger here. Once Black trades the bishop on c3, White recaptures toward the middle with a tempo and an open game, and there is even a tactic waiting if Black snatches the e4-pawn. Keep the pawn move in reserve.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O Bxc3 dxc3
teaches: When you recapture, prefer the direction that opens a piece and grips the centre over the one that merely keeps the pawns tidy — a recapture toward the middle frees a bishop and stakes a bigger central claim.
explains: You could take back the tidy way and keep the pawns clean — but take with the d-pawn instead. It opens the dark-squared bishop's diagonal and tightens White's grip on the central squares. The doubled pawns are a small price for that activity.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O Bxc3 dxc3 Nxe4 Nxe5
teaches: When the opponent grabs a pawn with a piece, look for the in-between capture that wins it straight back — and do not fear a desperado counter-grab. Counting the sequence out beats reflexively defending.
explains: If Black snatches the pawn on e4, don't scramble to defend — count it. The knight takes on e5, hitting the knight on c6, and White regains the material once the dust settles. A desperado counter-grab is nothing to fear when you have counted the line to the end.
